slides.title: Our starting hypothesis, a staged purchase of RouteSprout in 2027, fails four of five tests; customer protection is unproven

claims.claim: 1 · Affordable: ✖ Fail
evidence: What would have to be true: Cash stays at or above the $9.0M floor through 2028, and the earnout can be funded
Path B leaves $0.5M of headroom at signing, then falls to $7.2M–8.2M by end-2028; the $7.0M earnout has no funding source (p. 4–5)

claims.claim: 2 · Fairly priced: ✖ Fail
evidence: What would have to be true: The price rests on verified recurring revenue
3.75 times recognized ARR, not 2.5 times; bookings include multi-year value and pilots; no quality-of-earnings (QoE) review (p. 6)

claims.claim: 3 · Pays back: ✖ Fail
evidence: What would have to be true: Positive incremental contribution within a reasonable horizon
+$0.07M (base) or −$1.21M (low) a year while integration support runs; payback over 15 years (p. 7–8)

claims.claim: 4 · Protects customers: ? Unproven
evidence: What would have to be true: Renewals and 99.7% uptime survive integration
Churn rose from 12% to 21%, the case assumes 100% renewal, an early interface swap risks churn, and no cohort data exists (p. 9–10)

claims.claim: 5 · Beats the alternatives: ✖ Fail
evidence: What would have to be true: Better on cash, payback, continuity and execution
The partnership earns more below about $3.5M of routing ARR and risks at most $1.2M; building is slower but cheaper (p. 11–13)

claims.claim: Revised answer: partner now within the cash limits; buy only if set thresholds clear (p. 14–16)

slides.title: Neither acquisition path keeps cash above the $9.0M board floor once 18 months of operating losses are counted

claims.claim: Both acquisition paths end below the floor in both cases; the partnership and the build stay well above it
evidence: Lowest cash through end-2028 compared with the $9.0M floor, $M (below 0 = breach): D · Internal build 11.6 (base) / 11.6 (low); C · Partnership 13.8 / 13.8; B · Staged acquisition -0.835 / -1.795; A · Full cash acquisition -8.335 / -9.295
C assumes zero partner revenue (worst case); D assumes the full $3.4M is spent before launch
A and B include RouteSprout losses and integration-era support from an assumed July 2027 close (team assumption)

claims.claim: Path B closes $0.5M above the floor; 18 months of losses take cash to $8.2M, or $7.2M in the low case
evidence: Path B cash walk, base case, $M: Cash today 24; Upfront price 11; Integration 3.5; RouteSprout EBITDA 1.5; Integration-era support 1.275; Cross-sell gross profit 1.44; Board floor 8.165; Headroom -0.835

claims.claim: How the 18-month operating drag is built (base case): −$1.5M + −$1.3M + $1.4M = −$1.3M
evidence: RouteSprout EBITDA, −$1.0M a year (pack) × 1.5 years
integration-era support, $0.85M a year (pack) × 1.5 years
cross-sell gross profit: linear ramp to $2.4M, so half on average, at 80%
drag in the base case; −$2.3M in the low case ($0.8M cross-sell)

claims.claim: Path A breaks the $15.0M spend limit ($24.0M − $9.0M) on its own, leaving $2.0M before losses

slides.title: Path B's $0.5M margin also faces three unpriced cash calls: unscoped work, the integration cap and the $7.0M earnout

claims.claim: Operating losses before synergies: −$1.3M to −$2.3M over 18 months, which alone breaches the $9.0M floor (p. 4)
evidence: RouteSprout EBITDA is −$1.0M a year and integration-era support costs $0.85M a year; cross-sell is unsigned and ramps over time

claims.claim: Unscoped integration work: Every $1 of overrun is $1 below the floor; Path B's $3.5M estimate leaves $0.5M under the $4.0M cap
evidence: 30% of the integration work is not yet scoped, and the six-month plan assumes zero change-management delay

claims.claim: The $4.0M integration cap: If it counts: A = $4.0M + $1.3M = $5.3M and B = $3.5M + $1.3M = $4.8M, so both breach the cap; if not, it hits cash instead
evidence: The cap covers "systems migration and customer support"; the pack calls the $0.85M a year of support "another" cost, so it may count

claims.claim: The $7.0M earnout due in 2029: Cash is already below the floor at end-2028; the base-case run-rate contribution of $0.92M a year would need about 7.6 years to fund it
evidence: Payable after 2028 if growth and renewal tests pass; the CFO notes an earnout "does not eliminate future cash strain"

claims.claim: Uptime service credits: Not quantified in the pack; the risk only runs one way, and a full record migration makes it larger
evidence: Large customers need 99.7% uptime; a missed quarter triggers service credits and renewal risk the sellers leave out

claims.claim: Any deal must leave room for 18 months of losses, unscoped work and an earnout not paid in cash

slides.title: At 3.75 times recognized ARR, the $18.0M price is 50% above the sellers' 2.5 times, and the $4.8M ARR itself is unverified

claims.claim: 50% higher multiple on recognized ARR, Atlas's policy basis, than on bookings
evidence: Sellers: $18.0M ÷ $7.2M bookings = 2.5
Atlas finance: $18.0M ÷ $4.8M ARR = 3.75
Path B upfront only: $11.0M ÷ $4.8M ARR = 2.2917

claims.claim: Why $7.2M of bookings is the wrong denominator
evidence: Not recurring: the $7.2M counts multi-year contract value and one-off pilots as if they renew
Unverified: no QoE review or verified ARR schedule; the 42% growth stops before the last quarter
No earnings: EBITDA is −$1.0M (with founders' pay), so the price rests on revenue quality and synergies

claims.claim: Path B's total including the full earnout is also $18.0M, or 3.75 times ARR: the staged structure moves when the money is paid, not how much

slides.title: The $2.4M cross-sell is ARR, not EBITDA: after all costs it adds about $0.1M a year, and loses $1.2M in the low case

claims.claim: Annual run-rate incremental contribution to Atlas, $M a year, by end-2028
evidence: Sellers' pitch (as EBITDA): 2.40 / — (Seller pitch)
Cross-sell ARR, end-2028: 2.40 / 0.80 (Sales VP / finance)
× 80% gross margin: 1.92 / 0.64 (Pack §5)
− Integration-era support: −0.85 / −0.85 (Pack §5)
= Cross-sell contribution: 1.07 / −0.21
+ RouteSprout EBITDA: −1.00 / −1.00 (FY2026, flat)
= Integration-era contribution: 0.07 / −1.21 (Result)
Memo: after support ends: 0.92 / −0.36 (Assumption)

claims.claim: Still optimistic: at 21% logo churn about $1.0M of RouteSprout's $4.8M ARR is at risk each year
evidence: The bridge keeps the sellers' 100% renewal; logo churn is used as a proxy for revenue churn. No cost savings are assumed, as the pack instructs
The low case is the one finance considers plausible if the 21% churn persists and only signed trials convert

slides.title: Buying takes over 15 years to pay back (never in the low case), building about 5, and partnering risks at most $1.2M

claims.claim: A · Full cash acquisition: payback ≈24 years / never
evidence: Cash committed 22.0
Run-rate contribution +0.92 / −0.36 (+0.07 / −1.21 during integration)
22.0 ÷ 0.92; RouteSprout's losses absorb most of the cross-sell gross profit

claims.claim: B · Staged acquisition: payback ≈16 years (23 with earnout) / never
evidence: Cash committed 14.5 upfront + 7.0 earnout
Run-rate contribution +0.92 / −0.36 (same business)
Staging lowers upfront cash, not the total; the earnout is paid only in the base case

claims.claim: C · Partnership: payback ≈1.1 years / not within the two-year term
evidence: Cash committed 1.2 (two-year minimum)
Run-rate contribution +0.46 / −0.25 (after the 0.6 a year minimum)
Breaks even at $1.36M of routing ARR; worst-case loss $1.2M, about $0.5M over two years in the low case

claims.claim: D · Internal build: payback ≈5.3 years after launch
evidence: Cash committed 3.4 through 2028 + 0.4 a year operations
Run-rate contribution +0.64 from 2029 (low case not given)
1.3 × 80% − 0.4 = 0.64; assumes an on-time launch and displaces the compliance upgrade at an unestimated cost

claims.claim: Deliberately simple, as the board asked: no precise DCF from inputs we do not have
evidence: For C, routing ARR uses the same $0.8M–2.4M range at 80% margin and Atlas's 55% share; the partner offer is limited, so the low end is likelier

slides.title: RouteSprout's churn is rising and its revenue is concentrated, yet the sellers' case assumes every account renews

claims.claim: Logo churn rose from 12% to 21% in two years; the sellers' case assumes none
evidence: Annual customer logo churn: FY2024 0.12; FY2026 0.21; Sellers' case 0

claims.claim: 58% of ARR sits in 41 accounts, about $68K each against $7.5K for the other 269
evidence: FY2026 ARR by account group, $M: 41 large accounts 2.784; 269 other accounts 2.016

claims.claim: Concentration magnifies churn: losing a handful of the 41 large accounts would wipe out a year of cross-sell
People drive renewals: interviews found account managers, not routing features, drive renewal decisions, so RouteSprout's account managers matter as much as its code
Interface timing: the product VP warns that replacing RouteSprout's interface before large customers renew could add churn
No cohort data: we cannot tell whether churn sits in small or large accounts; this is the first diligence item

slides.title: The synergy, retention and integration claims rest on correlations and untested plans, not on evidence of cause

claims.claim: "Customers who use routing renew at 95%, so routing causes retention" — No retention uplift credited to Atlas's core base; keep RouteSprout's account managers
evidence: Routing users are mostly larger, multi-branch firms with dedicated customer-success teams; smaller non-users renew at 78%, so the feature effect is not isolated

claims.claim: "Integration works when the product is under one general manager" — Not transferable: we do not underwrite the $2.4M cross-sell, and earnouts carry that risk instead
evidence: The cited companies were on average twice as large, with lower churn; the link between integration spend and cross-sell is a correlation with no causal identification

claims.claim: "Six months and $4.0M to integrate" — Integrate through the API first; scope 100% of the work and price the contingency before signing
evidence: 30% of the work is unscoped and the plan assumes zero change-management delay; API plus single sign-on (SSO) is simpler than migrating records and support

claims.claim: "2.5x recurring revenue" and $7.2M of "annual recurring new sales" — Value on QoE-verified recognized ARR only
evidence: The $7.2M includes multi-year contract value and one-time pilots, so it is unsuitable for valuation or for projecting retention

claims.claim: Key people stay (implicit) — Signed 24-month retention agreements become a condition of the deal
evidence: A substantial part of the value depends on keeping key engineers for at least two years, and no agreements are in place

slides.title: Against the board's four criteria, only the partnership passes in 2027 — the build is the fallback, not the first move

claims.claim: A · Full cash acquisition fails cash, payback, customer continuity and execution; passes strategic fit
evidence: Cash: ✖ Fail: $22.0M out, cash at $2.0M before losses
Payback: ✖ Fail: about 24 years in the base case, never in the low case
Customer continuity: ✖ Fail: full migration before renewals, with churn at 21%
Execution: ✖ Fail: 30% unscoped, zero-delay plan, key engineers at risk
Strategic fit: ✔ Pass: owns routing and RouteSprout's team

claims.claim: B · Staged acquisition fails cash, payback and execution; watch on continuity; passes strategic fit
evidence: Cash: ✖ Fail: $14.5M at signing, then $7.2M–8.2M by end-2028
Payback: ✖ Fail: about 16 years (23 with the earnout), never in the low case
Customer continuity: ! Watch: same migration risk; the earnout ties sellers to renewals
Execution: ✖ Fail: same integration load on a thinner budget
Strategic fit: ✔ Pass: owns routing once integrated

claims.claim: C · Commercial partnership passes cash and continuity; watch on payback, execution and fit
evidence: Cash: ✔ Pass: at most $1.2M, cash stays at $22.8M or more
Payback: ! Watch: breaks even at $1.36M of routing ARR; loss capped at $1.2M
Customer continuity: ✔ Pass: no migration; prospects served from summer 2027
Execution: ! Watch: depends on the partner's viability; roadmap has to be shared
Strategic fit: ! Watch: no ownership, but first refusal keeps the option

claims.claim: D · Internal build passes cash; watch on payback and continuity; fails execution; passes strategic fit
evidence: Cash: ✔ Pass: $3.4M, cash stays at $20.6M or more
Payback: ! Watch: about 5.3 years after a late-2028 launch
Customer continuity: ! Watch: nothing to offer prospects until late 2028
Execution: ✖ Fail: at least 18 months, and it displaces the compliance upgrade
Strategic fit: ✔ Pass: Atlas owns the IP, but it arrives late

claims.claim: Only one routing strategy can run in 2027

slides.title: The partnership out-earns ownership at any routing ARR below about $3.5M, well above the Sales VP's unsigned $2.4M

claims.claim: Ownership wins only at scale: $3.5M routing ARR at which ownership first matches the partnership while integration support runs
evidence: Annual run-rate contribution by routing ARR $0.0M–$4.0M: Partnership -0.6; -0.38; -0.16; 0.06; 0.28; 0.5; 0.72; 0.94; 1.16
Acquisition, after support ends: -1; -0.6; -0.2; 0.2; 0.6; 1; 1.4; 1.8; 2.2
Partnership: 0.44 × ARR − 0.6 (55% of 80% gross profit, less the $0.6M a year minimum)
Acquisition: 0.8 × ARR − 1.85 while support runs ($1.0M losses, $0.85M support), 0.8 × ARR − 1.0 after; crossover 1.25 ÷ 0.36 = $3.47M at +0.93

claims.claim: Low and base cases: partner −0.25 against −1.21 at $0.8M; +0.46 against +0.07 at $2.4M
After support ends: the crossover is still $2.78M, once the partner minimum lapses too
Capital excluded: counting the $14.5M to $22.0M paid to acquire widens the partnership's lead
Assumption: partner-sold routing earns the same 80% margin; the $1.2M minimum is a sunk cost

slides.title: Building is affordable but cannot ship before late 2028, missing renewals the partnership serves from summer 2027

claims.claim: When each path delivers routing to customers, by quarter, March 2027 board to mid-2029
evidence: C · Partnership: Live summer 2027, two-year term to mid-2029
A/B · Acquisition: Diligence; Integrate (six-month plan); Delay risk
D · Internal build: Build, at least 18 months; Launch; Ramp to $1.3M ARR
Board, Mar 2027; Gate, Q1 2028
Timing assumptions: the acquisition closes after a roughly 3-month diligence; Atlas can run only one major routing strategy in 2027
The build starts after the March 2027 board and takes at least 18 months, so launch comes no earlier than Q4 2028

claims.claim: Cost: $3.4M through 2028, plus $0.4M a year in operations after launch
Return: $0.64M a year if $1.3M of ARR arrives (1.3 × 80% − 0.4), about 5.3 years to pay back; the pack's "2028 ARR" is unlikely after a late-2028 launch, so we treat it as a 2029 run-rate
Hidden cost: it displaces a planned compliance upgrade, at a customer cost not yet estimated
Role: the fallback if the partnership underperforms and the buy terms fail at the 2028 gate

slides.title: Sign the partnership on terms that cap cost, protect uptime and stop a competitor from capturing RouteSprout

claims.claim: Commercial terms cap the cost and protect uptime
evidence: Scope and price (as offered): non-exclusive routing API with a $1.2M two-year minimum; gross profit splits 55% to Atlas and 45% to RouteSprout
Ask, credit the minimum: count minimum payments against RouteSprout's 45% share, which cuts the $1.36M break-even and the $1.2M maximum loss
Service level: at least 99.7% quarterly uptime, with service credits passed back to Atlas to match the credits Atlas owes its large customers
Ask, segment exclusivity: exclusivity in utilities and repair contractors, Atlas's core segments; negotiate for it, but do not make it a condition

claims.claim: Protection terms stop a competitor capturing RouteSprout
evidence: Change of control: right of first refusal on any sale of RouteSprout, plus a right to terminate if a competitor buys it; the founders want to sell, so this is the key protection
Pre-agreed purchase option: attach the conditional term sheet (p. 15), exercisable at the Q1 2028 gate, with partnership fees credited against the price
Information rights: customer-level churn cohorts, the ARR schedule and pipeline data, which double as diligence evidence
Continuity and roadmap: source-code escrow and data portability in case RouteSprout fails (EBITDA −$1.0M); share only interface-level roadmap, through a clean team
Why walk away without them: the roadmap risk would then outweigh the speed benefit

claims.claim: Walk away if RouteSprout refuses first-refusal or change-of-control terms; reopen the build

slides.title: If evidence clears, buy conditionally: at most $8.5M upfront, up to $9.5M more if earned, never breaching the cash floor

claims.claim: Conditional term sheet limits and structure
evidence: Upfront cash: $8.5M — QoE-verified recognized ARR excluding pilots (about 1.8 times); cut about 1.8 times any shortfall; never raised
Earnout: $9.5M — Total within the sellers' $18.0M; 2028–29 tests: top-41 ARR kept, churn ≤ 12%, signed cross-sell in $1.4M–2.4M bands, 99.7% uptime
Payment protection: $9.0M floor + buffer — Paid only while cash stays above floor plus buffer; excess deferred, or in Atlas equity if shareholders approve
Integration: $4.0M cap — API and single sign-on first; no interface swap or record migration before large renewals; fully scoped, incl. support
People: 24 months — Retention agreements for key engineers and account managers, signed before close
Walk-away: Over $8.5M upfront or all cash — Keep the partnership and do not buy

claims.claim: Deriving the upfront ceiling: $15M − $4M − $2.3M = $8.7M maximum affordable; the $8.5M ceiling (about 1.8 times ARR) leaves a thin $0.2M buffer
evidence: $15M cash above the $9.0M floor
$4M integration at the $4.0M cap (30% unscoped, so assume all of it is used)
$2.3M 18-month operating drag, low case (losses + support − cross-sell gross profit)

claims.claim: The ceiling drops $1-for-$1 for partnership fees not credited at close and for any audited integration budget above the cap; never raise it to offset churn in large accounts

slides.title: Six pieces of missing information would change the recommendation, and each has a threshold set in advance

claims.claim: 1 · QoE-verified ARR
evidence: Today: $4.8M, unverified; bookings include pilots
Threshold: Recognized ARR of at least $4.8M, excluding pilots
If not met: Cut the price by about 1.8 times each $1 of shortfall, or walk away

claims.claim: 2 · Customer-level churn cohort
evidence: Today: 21% logo churn, no cohort data
Threshold: Churn falling toward the FY2024 level of 12%, and stable top-41 accounts
If not met: Stay with the partnership; do not buy

claims.claim: 3 · Signed routing demand
evidence: Today: $0 signed; $2.4M is the Sales VP's view
Threshold: At least $1.36M of run-rate shows demand; about $2.3M is needed to cover RouteSprout's losses
If not met: Below $1.36M, reconsider routing altogether, including the build

claims.claim: 4 · RouteSprout standalone EBITDA
evidence: Today: −$1.0M a year
Threshold: At breakeven, ownership needs only about $1.06M of cross-sell (0.85 ÷ 0.8)
If not met: Keep the earnout weighted to results

claims.claim: 5 · Audited integration budget
evidence: Today: 30% unscoped, zero-delay plan
Threshold: Fully scoped at no more than $4.0M, including support and contingency
If not met: Do not buy

claims.claim: 6 · Key people and seller terms
evidence: Today: No retention agreements; $18.0M all cash
Threshold: 24-month agreements signed, and sellers accept at most $8.5M upfront
If not met: Keep the partnership; revisit the build in 2028

claims.claim: Early trigger: if a rival bidder emerges, use first refusal only once items 1, 2 and 5 clear

slides.title: In March, approve the partnership, fund diligence and set walk-away terms; decide on buying at a Q1 2028 gate

claims.claim: Five decisions requested in March 2027
evidence: Decline the $18.0M all-cash proposal (Path A) and the staged deal as structured (Path B)
Approve the two-year RouteSprout partnership (at most $1.2M minimum) with the protections on p. 14
Approve preliminary diligence: QoE, customer cohorts, integration scoping and key-person review; the CFO sizes the budget, which the pack does not give
Mandate negotiation of the conditional term sheet: at most $8.5M upfront and up to $9.5M earned, with a set walk-away
Defer the internal build, and revisit it at the gate if the partnership underperforms

claims.claim: Sequence after approval
evidence: Apr–Jun 2027: sign the partnership; run diligence in parallel and negotiate the conditional term sheet
Summer 2027: routing goes live with the enterprise prospects that asked for it; track attach and ARR
Q3–Q4 2027: QoE and cohort results arrive; watch renewal outcomes for RouteSprout's 41 large accounts
Q1 2028 gate: buy if all six thresholds are met (p. 16); otherwise continue the partnership, or start the build if demand is proven but the partner falls short
Any time: if a competing bid emerges, apply the early trigger (p. 16)

claims.claim: Our reading: partnering in 2027, then buying in 2028, counts as one routing strategy

slides.title: The recommendation carries five main risks, each with a mitigation, and its cash downside is capped at $1.2M

claims.claim: RouteSprout is sold to a competitor during the partnership — Residual: Medium
evidence: Why: The founders want to sell, and Atlas will have shared roadmap details
Mitigation: Right of first refusal, termination on change of control, interface-only roadmap through a clean team
Residual: Atlas would lose its routing supplier, and the build becomes the fallback

claims.claim: The partner offering is too limited for enterprise prospects — Residual: Medium
evidence: Why: The partner offer is "limited", and prospects may want deep integration
Mitigation: Pilot with the requesting prospects in summer 2027 and measure attach before the gate
Residual: prospects may wait for the 2028 decision

claims.claim: Routing ARR stays below the $1.36M break-even — Residual: Low
evidence: Why: The $1.2M minimum is a fixed cost
Mitigation: Ask for the minimum to be credited against the 45% share; weight the gate to signed ARR
Residual: at most $1.2M, about $0.5M net in the low case

claims.claim: RouteSprout fails financially — Residual: Medium
evidence: Why: EBITDA is −$1.0M, churn is 21%, and its cash position is unknown
Mitigation: Source-code escrow, data portability and uptime service credits; our minimum also funds the partner
Residual: service disruption, so the SLA must be tied to 99.7%

claims.claim: The sellers reject the conditional terms — Residual: Low
evidence: Why: The founders asked for $18.0M in cash
Mitigation: Walk away: the partnership meets the customer need without ownership
Residual: we give up the option of owning routing, not the capability

slides.title: Appendix
BACKUP: The analysis separates pack evidence from assumptions, each one conservative or tested where it is used

claims.claim: Assumptions and evidence used, with sensitivity
evidence: Close timing — Assumption: July 2027, so 18 months to end-2028 — March board plus about 3 months of diligence; a later close shifts timing, not the conclusion
RouteSprout EBITDA — Assumption: held at −$1.0M a year — 42% growth and 21% churn pull opposite ways; breakeven cuts the cross-sell needed to about $1.06M (p. 16)
Cross-sell ramp — Assumption: linear from 0 to target by end-2028 — Average ARR over the period is half the target
Integration-era support — Evidence + assumption: $0.85M a year for 18 months, then ends — Amount from the pack, duration assumed; a cost to cash or to the $4.0M cap (p. 5)
Partner economics — Assumption: same ARR range at 80% margin; $1.2M minimum fixed — Conservative: crediting the minimum would improve the partnership case
Atlas core operations — Evidence: about cash-break-even — No offset from, or drain on, core cash
Synergies, retention uplift — Evidence + choice: none — The pack says not to assume savings; the routing-retention link is confounded
ARR at risk from churn — Assumption: 21% × $4.8M ≈ $1.0M a year — Logo churn as a proxy for revenue churn; not in the base numbers
One routing strategy — Interpretation: partnering, then buying, counts as one — If the board disagrees, the 2028 gate is partnership against build only

normalized.recommendation: Decline the $18.0M all-cash proposal (Path A) and the staged deal as structured (Path B); approve the two-year RouteSprout partnership (at most $1.2M minimum) with the protections on p. 14; approve preliminary diligence (QoE, customer cohorts, integration scoping and key-person review); mandate negotiation of the conditional term sheet: at most $8.5M upfront and up to $9.5M earned, with a set walk-away; defer the internal build, and revisit it at the gate if the partnership underperforms. Decide on buying at a Q1 2028 gate: buy if all six thresholds are met.

alternatives_considered.treatment: Rejected: breaks the $15.0M spend limit on its own ($22.0M out, cash at $2.0M before losses); payback about 24 years base, never in low case; fails cash, payback, customer continuity and execution; passes strategic fit. Decline the $18.0M all-cash proposal.

Rejected as structured: $14.5M at signing, then cash falls to $7.2M–8.2M by end-2028, below the $9.0M floor; $7.0M earnout unfunded; payback about 16 years (23 with earnout), never in low case; fails four of five tests, customer protection unproven.

Chosen: only option passing all four board criteria in 2027; at most $1.2M at risk, live summer 2027, no migration, out-earns ownership below about $3.5M of routing ARR; signed with first refusal, change-of-control and other protections.

Deferred as fallback: affordable ($3.4M) but cannot ship before late 2028, about 5.3 years payback, displaces the compliance upgrade; fails execution capacity. Revisit at the gate if the partnership underperforms.
Kept as an option: at most $8.5M upfront plus up to $9.5M earnout, only if six pre-set thresholds clear; walk away if over $8.5M upfront or all cash.

assumptions_and_uncertainties: Close timing assumed July 2027, so 18 months to end-2028; a later close shifts timing, not the conclusion
RouteSprout EBITDA held at −$1.0M a year; 42% growth and 21% churn pull opposite ways
Cross-sell ramps linearly from 0 to target by end-2028, so average ARR is half the target
Integration-era support of $0.85M a year assumed to last 18 months, then end; may count against the $4.0M integration cap
Partner economics: same ARR range at 80% margin; $1.2M minimum fixed (conservative)
No synergies or retention uplift assumed; the routing-retention link is confounded
ARR at risk from churn: 21% × $4.8M ≈ $1.0M a year; logo churn used as proxy for revenue churn; not in the base numbers
The bridge keeps the sellers' 100% renewal
Interpretation that partnering then buying counts as one routing strategy; if the board disagrees, the 2028 gate is partnership against build only
Partnership worst case assumes zero partner revenue; build case assumes full $3.4M spent before launch
30% of integration work is unscoped and the plan assumes zero change-management delay
$4.8M ARR is unverified; no QoE review or cohort data
Uptime service credits not quantified in the pack
Build low case not given; build displaces compliance upgrade at an unestimated cost
Diligence budget not given in the pack; CFO to size it
Payback is deliberately simple and undiscounted; no precise DCF
Main risks: RouteSprout sold to a competitor; partner offering too limited; routing ARR below $1.36M break-even; RouteSprout fails financially; sellers reject conditional terms
